newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber falls to 10-wk lows, losses then pared.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber falls to 10-wk lows, losses then pared.

text.p: Carryover selling from Tuesday's limit losses and continued weakness in cash lumber knocked CME lumber futures down to 10-week lows before finding short covering support, traders said.

Carryover sell stops and selling linked to declining cash lumber prices took July down to $366 per thousand board feet, its lowest level since March 26. Slow demand and more than adequate production has weighed on the cash spruce market and futures in turn, turned down after gains on Monday, traders said.
However, futures are looking oversold which limited the setback after initial losses, they added.
Random Lengths early Wednesday officially quoted cash spruce at $362, off $2 from last Friday.
At 0925 CDT, lumber stood $5.50 lower to $0.80 higher with only November up and July off most at $368.00 per tbf. September was off $1.40 at $361.60 per tbf.
Oriented strand board lumber quickly ran into resistance after closing up the daily limit Tuesday following reports of a fire destroying an OSB mill. The market looks overbought, traders said.
OSB is trading $0.50 to $6.00 lower with July off the least at $148.00 per 1,000 square ft.
